detail.body:
## Overview

Reject unresolved multimodal features before worker admission, including when
prefix, encoder, or external encoder caches are warm. Layout-only requests to
`/inference/v1/generate` return HTTP 400 before submission to the engine.

## Claims

- Validate every feature once in `EngineCore.preprocess_add_request`, after
  receiver-cache lookup; unresolved items raise `MultiModalCacheMissError`.
- Preserve valid receiver-cache hits and existing EC metadata inputs.
- Remove the scheduler guards, repeated cache queries, and zero-token returns.
- Return HTTP 400 for scale-out features with neither payload nor metadata,
  including streaming requests. Render with `mm_payload: "tensors"` to include
  the payload.

## Validation

- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=. HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_mm_serde.py -q --tb=short`: **307 passed**.
- Admission tests cover LLaVA and Qwen2-VL with cold cache, future chunk input,
  encoder hit, EC hit, prefix hit, and receiver hit. The Qwen encoder-hit test
  fails without the new guard because admission does not raise the typed error.
- HTTP tests exercise the actual FastAPI route with whole-field and per-item
  null payloads, both streaming and non-streaming.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Repository-wide pre-commit: unrelated macOS failures for Linux-only APIs in
  mypy and `/var` versus `/private/var` in the non-root entrypoint wrapper.
- GPU end-to-end: **pending**. Added
  `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_multimodal_tokens.py::test_layout_only_features_return_bad_request_and_server_recovers`
  to the existing Buildkite entrypoints suite. It verifies layout-only render
  output receives HTTP 400 and subsequent rendering with tensors generates
  successfully on Qwen3-VL. This test has not been run locally.
- No model evaluation was run: successful-request model outputs and sampling
  are unchanged; the change rejects unresolved inputs.

## Details

Encoder outputs and cached prefix tokens do not supply the feature data used
by M-RoPE setup during worker admission. Allowing a null item through on those
cache hits still reaches model assertions. Receiver-cache resolution must run
first, then every unresolved feature must be rejected before scheduling.

The HTTP path now rejects layout-only features before calling the engine.
For direct engine callers, the guard reuses the existing typed cache-miss path.
General generation cache-miss recovery is handled separately in #61656; this
revision does not duplicate its output-processor or endpoint retry changes.
The explicit continuation contract in #60526 is separate from ordinary
multimodal admission. Both related diffs were checked before this revision.

Public `/generate` callers must now supply payload data or the existing EC
metadata contract for each feature. Hashes and placeholder positions alone are
insufficient. Internal receiver-cache references still resolve normally.

AI assistance was used to develop and review this revision. The human submitter
reviewed the changes and approved pushing with GPU end-to-end validation pending.

---

## Rebase validation — 2026-10-27

Rebased onto upstream main, preserving the original fix and current surrounding behavior. The duplicate audit found no complete merged or open replacement for this PR’s remaining control.

Preserved upstream scheduler tests. The broad run had 365 passes and four failures; the same four fail on clean upstream because of unavailable model/configuration support in this CPU environment.

Validation on macOS CPU: **365 passed; four unrelated failures also reproduced on clean upstream were excluded from the final run**. All applicable changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' PYTHONPATH=. HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_mm_serde.py -k 'not streaming_lookahead_hashes_follow_recomputed_kv and not async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders' -q --tb=short -p no:cacheprovider
```

Native GPU/RDMA execution and model evaluations were not run during this rebase; required CI and human review remain pending. AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for the conflict resolution and validation.

inline_comments.body:
The `mm_end <= num_computed_tokens skip` and the encoder cache / EC connector `continue` below only skip the encoder. The worker still calls `get_mrope_input_positions` on every feature at admission and `qwen2_vl.py:1327` does `assert data is not None`. So with a warm cache this still crashes. 22 models implement `get_mrope_input_positions`.

Simplest fix is to reject any `data=None` item at admission and drop these allowances. If we need to keep them, at least reject when `model_config.uses_mrope` is set.

reviews.body:
## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks @jperezdealgaba for picking this up. The guard covers the basic case but I don't think it closes the issue yet.                                                                                        

The cache hit paths (prefix cache, encoder cache, EC connector) still let a `data=None` item reach the worker. On M-RoPE models like Qwen2-VL, the worker reads `mm_feature.data` in `add_request` whatever the cache state is. Those paths therefore still take the engine down. Inline comments have the details.

The client also still gets a 500. I'd rather this come back as a 4xx or reuse the retryable `multimodal_cache_miss` error.

Thanks @jperezdealgaba. A few things before this can merge:

- Please answer @DarkLight1337's question on `core.py`. The receiver cache only exists on the engine for LRU, so a one line comment saying that should do it.
- `test_admission_requires_resolved_multimodal_data` can be shortened. The check never reads scheduler or cache state which means one rejected case and one receiver hit cover it. `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py` looks like a better home also.
- The `mm_payload` field descriptions in the chat, completion, responses and anthropic `protocol.py` files still say a null `kwargs_data` means every item is cached.

One question on EC prefill. LLaVA renders `mm_metadata: null` and as far as I can tell the documented prefill flow in `renderer.md` (drop `kwargs_data`, send `ec_transfer_params`) now gets a 400 on models like that. Is that intended? If it is, can you document it? If not, could reject only when `uses_mrope` is set.
